task_instance: QA a sample SRT caption file against the Netflix English (adult) standard: measure every cue for reading speed (cps), line length, line count, time on screen, and inter-cue gaps/overlaps, report pass/fail counts, and gate with a non-zero exit code suitable for CI.
evidence: Wrote a 6-cue sample.srt in the work directory containing deliberate violations of each rule, plus the reference check_captions.py from the SKILL.md verbatim (needs only Python 3; no network, no installs). Ran: cd <work>; python3 check_captions.py sample.srt. The script output flagged each category correctly: cue 2 '220.0 characters a second; line 1 is 66 characters; on screen 0.30 s'; cue 3 '20.4 characters a second; ... gap of 1 frames at 24 fps'; cue 4 'overlaps the next caption by 0.50 s'; cue 5 'line 1 is 49 characters'; cue 6 '125.0 characters a second; line 1 is 88 characters; 3 lines'. Summary line 'sample.srt: 1 of 6 captions pass' and process exit code 1 (would fail a build). Verified by hand: cue 2 body is 66 chars over 0.30 s = 220 cps; cue 4 out-time 12.000 vs cue 5 in-time 11.500 = 0.50 s overlap. The core deliverable (standard-based caption lint/QA with per-cue failure report and CI gate) exists and runs. Files produced: <work>/check_captions.py, <work>/sample.srt, <work>/result.json. Python 3.13.17.
